tools.name: check_building
tools.description: Checks whether BuzzMeBro can give this building a local buzzer number, and returns the price, the free-trial terms and how the service works. Call this first. Stores nothing and costs nothing.

tools.name: create_setup
tools.description: Creates a BuzzMeBro setup for the person and returns setup_id and a status_token you must keep for every later call (plus setup_url, a fallback link if you cannot relay a texted code). Only call it after check_building said available and the person has asked you to set it up. No text message is sent

tools.name: send_phone_code
tools.description: Texts a 6-digit code to the mobile number given in create_setup (never to any other number). Tell the person a text is coming and ask them to read the code to you, then call confirm_phone_code. Call again only if it has not arrived after a minute; each setup gets 3 codes.

tools.name: confirm_phone_code
tools.description: Checks the code the person read back to you. This proves the phone is theirs, which matters because that phone will open their front door. Five tries per setup. Next: start_checkout.

tools.name: start_checkout
tools.description: After confirm_phone_code: creates the person’s BuzzMeBro account and apartment and returns payment_url, Stripe’s own secure page where the person approves a card, Apple Pay, Google Pay or Link (with the free month when it applies, nothing is charged until it ends). Give them the link or message_for_

tools.name: get_setup_status
tools.description: Reads how far the setup has got and says what to do next. Once the person has paid, this call gets their number; when status is "ready" it returns their new BuzzMeBro number and swap_the_buzzer: the steps to get the building to point the buzzer at that number, and ready-to-send messages for building

tools.name: partner_program_info
tools.description: Returns how the partner program works: the 50% share of collected revenue, what counts and what does not, when and how payouts happen, the rules, and the steps to join. Call it first and explain it to the person before applying. Stores nothing.

tools.name: partner_apply
tools.description: Starts a partner application with the person’s details and returns application_id and application_token. Only call it when the person has asked to join. No text is sent by this call. Next: partner_send_code.

tools.name: partner_send_code
tools.description: Texts a 6-digit code to the mobile number in the application (never any other number). Ask the person to read it to you, then call partner_confirm_code. Each application gets 3 codes, at least a minute apart.

tools.name: partner_confirm_code
tools.description: Checks the texted code. Five tries per application. Next: partner_terms_link.

tools.name: partner_terms_link
tools.description: Returns a one-time link to the partner terms. Give it to the person: they read the terms and press Accept themselves. You cannot accept for them. When they say it is done, call partner_claim_key.

tools.name: partner_claim_key
tools.description: After the person accepted the terms: returns their partner link, code and partner key. The key is shown once; keep it private and use it for the partner_get_* tools. The application token stops working after this call.

tools.name: partner_get_links
tools.description: Returns the partner’s share link, typed code, a QR code (SVG) and their dashboard address.

tools.name: partner_get_kit
tools.description: Returns ready texts, a resident email, desk card and move-in insert wording with the partner’s link, plus the house rules for sharing (honest words only, no pressure, never ask residents for phone numbers or door codes).

tools.name: partner_get_stats
tools.description: Returns status, visits, signups, free months, paying apartments, collected revenue, earnings by state (on hold, ready, paid, reversed), the share ledger (apartments as codes only, never names or addresses) and payout history. Quote only these numbers.

tools.name: partner_payout_link
tools.description: Returns a one-time link to a BuzzMeBro page that sends the person to Stripe’s own secure page, where THEY confirm their identity and add their bank. You never see or type bank details. Payouts start once they have at least $25 ready.

tools.name: partner_rotate_key
tools.description: Revokes the current partner key and returns a new one (shown once). Use it if the key may have leaked.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "confirm_phone_code" appears informational but accepts parameters (code) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_setup_status, partner_get_kit · Private data: partner_claim_key · Public sink: send_phone_code, get_setup_status, partner_program_info, partner_send_code, partner_get_links, partner_get_kit, partner_get_stats.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_setup_status, partner_get_kit · Private data: partner_claim_key · Public sink: send_phone_code, get_setup_status, partner_program_info, partner_send_code, partner_get_links, partner_get_kit, partner_get_stats

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
